indicator_definition: This indicator measures total greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from the agricultural sector, expressed in million tonnes of CO₂ equivalent. Agricultural emissions include methane from livestock and manure management, nitrous oxide from soils and carbon dioxide from on-farm energy use.
rationale: Agriculture contributes significantly to total greenhouse gas emissions. Reducing agricultural emissions while maintaining food production is a key challenge for meeting climate targets. Progress means a reduction in total GHG emissions from agriculture without compromising food security.
methodology_characteristics: Data are reported by national authorities under the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) and compiled by Eurostat. Emissions are estimated using IPCC methodology and cover all agricultural emission sources including enteric fermentation, manure management and agricultural soils.
